chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Mutamatti' who performed Tawaf with the House and between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and kissed his wife before shortening his hair, and he said: 'Upon him is a blood offering which he must shed, and if intercourse occurred, upon him is the blood of a camel or a cow.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: As-Safa and Al-Marwah, the hills between which pilgrims walk during Sa'i
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: To shorten or cut (referring to the ritual hair cutting/shaving)
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُهُ: He must shed (pour out the blood of the sacrificed animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who has sexual intercourse before shaving his head?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific fidya for a Mutamatti' who engages in marital intimacy before the final shaving (Qasr), distinguishing between mere kissing and full intercourse. The ruling prescribes a general blood offering (dam) for kissing, while requiring the heavier sacrifice of a camel or cow for sexual intercourse, reflecting the gradation of the breach of the ihram sanctity. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise expiation based on the nature of the act during the state of consecration.
